title: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Current
summary: ## Faraday's laws
Magnetic flux φ = BA cos θ, measured in webers.
First law: an emf is induced in a coil whenever the magnetic flux linked with it changes; the cause is the change in flux.
Second law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage, e = −N dφ/dt.
Lenz's law gives the direction: the induced current opposes the change that produces it, which is a consequence of conservation of energy.
Motional emf: e = Blv. A rod of length l rotating with angular speed ω (frequency ν) in a field B has e = ½Bωl² = πνBl².

Eddy currents are induced in bulk conductors. A magnet falling through a copper tube is slowed by them. They are used in induction furnaces, speedometers and electromagnetic brakes, and reduced by laminating transformer cores.
## Self and mutual induction
Self-inductance: e = −L dI/dt. For a solenoid L = μ₀N²A/l, measured in henry. Mutual inductance is the basis of the transformer.
## Alternating current
e = e₀ sin ωt, with ω = 2πν. The rms value is peak/√2.

Pure resistor: V and I are in phase. Pure inductor: X_L = ωL and the voltage leads the current by π/2. Pure capacitor: X_C = 1/ωC and the current leads the voltage by π/2. The average power in a pure L or pure C is zero.
Series LCR circuit: Z = √[R² + (X_L − X_C)²] and tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R. If X_C > X_L the current leads the voltage. At resonance X_L = X_C, ν₀ = 1/2π√(LC), Z = R and the power factor cos φ = 1.
Example: L = 60 mH, C = 50 µF, R = 20 Ω and ω = 400 rad/s give X_L = 24 Ω, X_C = 50 Ω and Z ≈ 32.8 Ω.
A coil carrying 1 A on 100 V dc but only 0.6 A on 100 V ac has R = 100 Ω and Z ≈ 167 Ω, so X_L ≈ 133 Ω. Inductive reactance reduces the ac current.
## Transformer

A transformer works by mutual induction and changes ac voltage. Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ = Iₚ/Iₛ for an ideal transformer. A step-up transformer has Nₛ > Nₚ; a step-down transformer has Nₛ < Nₚ. Efficiency η = P_out/P_in.
Energy losses: copper loss (I²R), eddy currents (reduced by a laminated core), hysteresis (reduced by a soft-iron core) and flux leakage.
Examples: 240 V to 12 V needs Nₚ : Nₛ = 20 : 1, with Iₚ : Iₛ = 1 : 20. 100 : 500 turns with 120 V and 3 A gives 600 V and 0.6 A.
An ac generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction.

vsa: A bar falling through the hollow region of a thick copper cylinder experiences a retarding force. What can you conclude about the bar? Explain.
The bar is a magnet. As it falls, the changing flux induces eddy currents in the copper which, by Lenz's law, oppose its motion — hence the retarding force. An unmagnetised bar would fall freely.
State Lenz's law. Show that it follows from conservation of energy.

The induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change producing it. If it aided the change, a small motion would produce ever-growing current and energy from nothing; opposing it means work must be done, which becomes electrical energy.
A coil carries 1 A on 100 V dc and 0.6 A on 100 V ac. Explain, and find its reactance.

On dc only resistance acts: R = 100/1 = 100 Ω. On ac the inductive reactance also acts: Z = 100/0.6 ≈ 167 Ω.
X_L = √(Z² − R²) = √(167² − 100²) ≈ 133 Ω.
State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction.

First law: whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced in it.
Second law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage: e = −N dφ/dt.
sa: State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction and explain them with an example.

First law: an emf is induced whenever the flux linked with a coil changes. Second law: e = −N dφ/dt.
Example: pushing a bar magnet into a coil connected to a galvanometer gives a deflection. Pulling it out deflects the other way, and moving it faster gives a bigger deflection. When the magnet is still there is no deflection, because the flux is not changing.
A transformer is to run machines needing (i) 25000 V and (ii) 25 V from a 250 V, 50 Hz supply. Name the transformers and give their turns ratios.

(i) Step-up transformer, Nₚ : Nₛ = 250 : 25000 = 1 : 100.
(ii) Step-down transformer, Nₚ : Nₛ = 250 : 25 = 10 : 1.
The primary is connected to the supply and the secondary to the machine.
What is a transformer? How does it work? Give three causes of energy loss in it.

A device that changes ac voltage (step up or step down) using mutual induction.
Working: ac in the primary makes a changing flux in the laminated soft-iron core, which induces an emf in the secondary: Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ.
Losses: (1) copper loss I²R in the windings; (2) eddy-current loss in the core; (3) hysteresis loss; also flux leakage.
la: A transformer has 200 turns in its primary and 1000 in its secondary, with resistances 0.4 Ω and 2 Ω. The secondary output is 13.5 kW at 1200 V and the efficiency is 90%. Find (i) the input voltage, (ii) the input power, (iii) the primary and secondary currents and (iv) the power lost in the primary.

(i) Vₚ = Vₛ × Nₚ/Nₛ = 1200 × 200/1000 = 240 V.
(ii) P_in = P_out/η = 13500/0.9 = 15000 W = 15 kW.
(iii) Iₚ = P_in/Vₚ = 15000/240 = 62.5 A; Iₛ = P_out/Vₛ = 13500/1200 = 11.25 A.
(iv) Primary copper loss = Iₚ²Rₚ = 62.5² × 0.4 ≈ 1562.5 W.
Total loss = 1500 W = 10% of the input.

la: A metal rod of length l rotates with frequency ν about one end, which is at the centre of a circular metal ring, the other end touching the ring. A uniform field B is parallel to the axis. Obtain the emf between the centre and the ring.

Take an element dr at distance r; its speed is v = ωr. The emf across it is de = Bv dr = Bωr dr.
e = ∫₀ˡ Bωr dr = ½Bωl².
With ω = 2πν: e = πνBl².
An ac voltage e = e₀ sin ωt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Draw the phasor diagram and obtain the impedance and the phase angle. When is the current maximum?

The same current I flows through all three. V_R is in phase with I, V_L leads I by 90° and V_C lags I by 90°.
From the phasor diagram: V² = V_R² + (V_L − V_C)² ⇒ Z = √[R² + (X_L − X_C)²], with X_L = ωL and X_C = 1/ωC.
Phase angle: tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R.
The current is maximum at resonance, X_L = X_C, i.e. ω₀ = 1/√(LC), when Z = R.
